title: Air Duct Cleaning Advertising: What Works and Examples (2026)
summary: Air duct cleaning advertising: the coupon offers, video and message ads that keep running, sample copy and how to measure cost per job.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Air duct cleaning is an impulse purchase. The ads that keep running stack a low entry price with a free extra, such as dryer vent cleaning or an AC tune-up, and mention allergies and dust.
- Roughly half the ads on the[air duct cleaning ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/air-duct-cleaning-ads) are video, and the most common call to action is Send message, so fast replies matter as much as the creative.
- Best channels: Google Search for people already looking, Meta for the coupon impulse, and a complete Google Business Profile for trust.
- Measure cost per completed job and the upsell rate behind it, not leads or clicks.


## What the ads that keep running have in common


The[air duct cleaning ads page](https://www.sprites.ai/air-duct-cleaning-ads) shows 68 live Meta ads from 12 advertisers. About 53% are video. The median ad has been running for 112 days, which is a long time for a paid ad, and the most common call to action is Send message, used on 25% of ads. The longest-running ads share a few traits.


- **A price or discount in the first line.** One opener reads "10% Off Residential DUCT CLEANING." Another is just "Air Duct Cleaning Special," and it has been live for 1,462 days. The offer is the hook.
- **A bundle.** One ad runs "THIS MONTH ONLY FULL AIR DUCT CLEANING + FREE AC TUNE-UP FOR $$99!!" for 388 days. A cheap cleaning plus a free second service makes the price feel small.
- **A health or dust question.** Openers such as "Is the air inside your home polluted or dirty?" point at something the homeowner cannot see. The deal then makes the call feel low risk.
- **Local or seasonal framing.** One of the longest-running ads addresses a whole state and says it is time to freshen up the house and clean the furnace ductwork. Another opens with "Attention Homeowners."
- **Video and a message button.** Video shows the dirty vent and the vacuum hose. A message button lets the homeowner ask a question without picking up the phone.


None of this is complicated. Duct cleaning is rarely on a to-do list. People buy it when an ad makes it cheap and easy enough to say yes today.


## Build the offer first


The offer does most of the work in air duct cleaning advertising. Creative only carries it. A strong offer has four parts.


Part What it does Example


Entry price Makes the first call feel low risk Whole-home duct cleaning for $99


Free add-on Raises perceived value without lowering the headline price Free dryer vent cleaning or free AC tune-up


Reason to care Gives the homeowner a motive beyond the coupon Allergies, pets, dust on furniture, a recent remodel or move


Deadline Turns "someday" into "this month" This month only, limited spots per week


Set the entry price by what the job costs you, not by what competitors show. Define what it covers: number of vents, square footage cap, one HVAC system. A $99 special that covers up to 10 vents and one system protects your margin. The same price with no limits does not.


### Work out whether the coupon pays


Here is an example. Replace the numbers with yours.


- Ad spend: $1,500 in a month.
- Booked and completed jobs: 30. Cost per completed job: $50.
- Revenue per job: $99 for the special. Half of customers add a $60 upgrade such as sanitizing or a dryer vent add-on. Average revenue: $129.
- Direct cost per job (labor, fuel, supplies): $75. Gross profit: $54.


After a $50 ad cost, the first job leaves $4. That is not a failure. It means the coupon is a customer acquisition cost, and the profit comes from the upgrade rate, the tune-up that turns into a repair, and the maintenance plan or repeat clean later. If the upgrade rate drops to 25%, the first job loses money. Track that number weekly.


## Air duct cleaning ad examples


### Meta ad: video plus message


**Video:** 20 to 30 seconds. Show the tech pulling a vent cover, the dust inside, the vacuum running and a clean result. Add captions, since many people watch without sound.


**Primary text:** "Sneezing more indoors than outside? Dust builds up in your ducts for years. This month, whole-home duct cleaning is $99 and we add a free dryer vent cleaning. Up to 10 vents, one system. Message us your ZIP code and we will send open times." **Headline:** "Duct cleaning from $99." **Button:** Send message.


### Meta ad: AC tune-up bundle


"Full air duct cleaning plus a free AC tune-up for $99, until the end of the month. Two services, one visit. Message us to claim a spot." This version suits companies that also do HVAC. See[Facebook ads for HVAC companies](https://www.sprites.ai/facebook-ads-for-hvac-companies) for how those businesses structure campaigns.


### Google Search ad


Responsive search ads allow headlines up to 30 characters and descriptions up to 90. A starting set:


Element Copy Characters


Headline 1 Air Duct Cleaning in Tampa 26


Headline 2 Full Duct Cleaning $99 22


Headline 3 Free Dryer Vent Cleaning 24


Headline 4 Licensed and Insured Techs 26


Description 1 Whole-home duct cleaning with a free dryer vent cleaning. Book online or call today. 83


Keep each headline able to stand alone, because Google mixes them. Search ads catch people who already want the service, so they can lead with licensing and fast scheduling. Meta ads need the deal and the dust.


## Which channels bring air duct cleaning leads


1. **Google Search.** People searching "air duct cleaning near me" are ready to book. Target your service area by ZIP code, add negative keywords such as "DIY" and "jobs," and send clicks to a page with the price, the offer and a phone number. The[Google Ads guide for carpet cleaners](https://www.sprites.ai/google-ads-for-carpet-cleaners) covers a similar impulse service.
2. **Facebook and Instagram.** Best for the coupon impulse. The ads on the wall lean on video and message buttons. Target homeowners in your service radius and keep the offer in the first line.
3. **Google Local Services Ads.** Pay-per-lead listings with a verification badge, where eligible. Eligibility depends on category and location, so check Google's current list. Our[Local Services Ads guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) explains setup.
4. **Google Business Profile.** Photos of dirty and clean ducts, reviews and service areas. It costs nothing and affects who gets the call.
5. **Direct mail and door hangers.** A coupon in the mailbox suits an impulse purchase. Use a unique phone number or QR code so you can count responses.
6. **HVAC partners.** Furnace installers and realtors send customers who have just moved or replaced equipment. See[HVAC marketing](https://www.sprites.ai/hvac-marketing) for related ideas.


## Handle message leads fast


When the top call to action is Send message, the ad is only half the work. A homeowner who messages at 8 p.m. is comparing two or three companies. The first one to reply with a price and open times usually gets the job.


- Reply within minutes during business hours, and set an automatic reply outside them.
- Ask three questions: ZIP code, number of vents or home size, and one or two systems.
- Offer two specific time slots instead of asking when they are free.
- Confirm what the special covers before the visit so the tech does not argue about the price at the door.
- Log every message as booked, lost or no reply. That is the data you need to judge the ad.


## Creative checklist


- Put the price or discount in the first line.
- Show real dust from a real vent, not stock images of a smiling family.
- Mention allergies, pets or dust in plain words, without medical promises.
- Name the city or county in the copy.
- Use one deadline you actually honor.
- Refresh the video every few months, even if the offer stays the same.


## How to measure air duct cleaning advertising


Track four numbers by channel: leads, booked jobs, completed jobs and revenue per completed job including upgrades. Divide spend by completed jobs for your real cost per job. Then compare it with gross profit per job and the share of customers who buy an upgrade or return. A channel with cheap leads and a low show rate can cost more per job than a pricier channel with better ones. ## FAQ


### What is the best way to advertise an air duct cleaning business?


Combine Google Search for people already looking with Meta ads built on a coupon offer. Use a low entry price, a free add-on and a deadline, and send leads to a message button or phone number you answer fast.


### How do you get more air duct cleaning leads?


Make the offer stronger and reply faster. Bundle the cleaning with a free dryer vent cleaning or AC tune-up, mention dust and allergies, and answer messages in minutes. Add a complete Google Business Profile and local reviews.


### Do Facebook ads work for air duct cleaning?


They can, because duct cleaning is an impulse buy and a coupon prompts the decision. The ads on the[air duct cleaning ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/air-duct-cleaning-ads) lean on video and message buttons, and the median ad has run 112 days. Judge your own by cost per completed job.


### What should an air duct cleaning ad say?


Open with the price or the bundle, name a reason to care such as dust or allergies, state what the special covers and add a deadline. End with one action, such as sending a message with a ZIP code.


### How much should an air duct cleaning company spend on ads?


Start from your gross profit per job. If a $99 special leaves about $54 and you expect half of customers to upgrade, your ad cost per completed job must stay near or under that. Increase spend only where the math holds.
